name: Box jump and depth jump
pattern: Jump up onto a box from a quick dip and arm swing, or step off a box and rebound: the legs load and explode, then land softly.
setup: Stand an arm's length from a stable box, feet hip width.
Pick a height you can land on in a quarter squat, not a deep squat.
Arms relaxed by your sides, weight on the balls of your feet.

steps.text: Swing your arms back and dip quickly into a quarter squat.
Swing your arms up and drive through hips, knees and ankles.
Pull your knees up to clear the edge of the box.
Land quietly with both feet flat, knees bent and over your toes.
Stand tall on the box, then step down, one foot at a time.

cues.cue: Land soft and quiet, knees and hips bent.
cues.why: Bending the knees and hips on landing lowers the impact force; people land softer once taught to.

cues.cue: Knees over your toes, not caving in.
cues.why: Knees that cave in on landing are linked to a higher risk of knee ligament injury.

cues.cue: Big arm swing back then up.
cues.why: An arm swing adds height to a jump through several mechanisms working together.

cues.cue: Choose a box you land on in a quarter squat.
cues.why: Landing deep means the box is too high: you are measuring hip mobility, not the jump.

cues.cue: Step down, do not jump down (unless it is a depth jump).
cues.why: Stepping off a box loads the legs more than landing from a jump of the same height.

breathing: Breathe in on the dip, out as you jump.

tempo.note: One max effort jump, then step down and reset; rest a few seconds between reps.

mistakes.name: Stiff landing
mistakes.looks: The legs stay nearly straight on contact and the landing is loud.
mistakes.fix: Land on the balls of the feet rolling to flat, sink the hips back.
mistakes.why: A stiff landing raises impact forces on the knee.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: From the front the knees fall toward each other on landing or take-off.
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the second toe; lower the box.
mistakes.why: Greater knee valgus on landing predicted ACL injury in young female athletes.

mistakes.name: Landing in a deep squat
mistakes.looks: Feet reach the box only with hips below the knees.
mistakes.fix: Use a lower box and jump higher.
mistakes.why: The box, not the jump, sets the height and the landing is out of balance.

safety: Use a stable box with a soft edge; start low.
Plyometrics on fresh legs, low volume: stop when landings get loud.
Knee or Achilles pain: switch to lower jumps or step-ups.

variants.change: Step off a low box (30-45 cm), land, and rebound up as fast as you can. Short ground contact; much higher knee loading than a box jump.
Stand beside the box and jump sideways onto it.
Take off and land on one leg; much lower box.
Start kneeling, swing the arms and jump to the feet, then to the box.
Turn 90-180° in the air before landing.
Depth jump into a hurdle hop or forward jump.
Upper body depth jump: drop from a raised surface to the hands and rebound.

subtypes.name: Depth or drop jump
subtypes.change: Step off the box, land on both feet, rebound up at once.

subtypes.name: Lateral box jump
subtypes.change: Side-on to the box; same dip and swing, jump sideways.

subtypes.name: Single-leg box jump
subtypes.change: One-leg take-off and landing on a low box, free knee bent.

easier: squat jump onto a low box

metrics.label: Knee cave on landing (front view)
metrics.good: under 13 and even on both sides

motion.basis: Landing targets from padua2009 (knee over 30° at contact, soft landing) and herrington2010 (normal drop-jump valgus about 7-13°); valgus risk from hewett2005 and ford2003; arm swing from lees2004. Keyframe angles are estimates, not measured values.
